projects.name: Project Cannoli

projects.name: Research computing center

projects.name: Beaver Dam data center

projects.name: Menomonie data center

projects.name: Town of Beloit data center
projects.fight: Residents requested a moratorium in June 2026; the town board now requires approval before officials sign NDAs.

projects.name: Cassville data center
projects.fight: Residents voted 54-3 to adopt village powers, and the town approved a two-year moratorium in spring 2026.

projects.name: DeForest data center
projects.fight: The village declared the project not feasible in January 2026 after resident opposition and a negative state annexation finding.

projects.name: Wisconsin Rapids data center complex (200+ acres)
Project Sail

projects.name: Project Peach

projects.name: Douglas County data center campus (4.4M sq ft)

projects.name: Bolingbroke data center (900+ acres)

projects.name: QTS Augusta

projects.name: Project Camellia

projects.name: Hampton data center (South Lee Rd and Lower Woolsey Rd)

projects.name: AWS Susquehanna campus (part of $20B Pennsylvania plan)

projects.name: AWS Falls Township campus (part of $20B Pennsylvania plan)

projects.name: Devil's Mountain site (up to 10 buildings)
projects.fight: Residents are pushing for a moratorium; the township limited public comment to residents.

projects.name: Project Scott

projects.name: Wildcat Ridge Data Center Campus

projects.name: Project Gravity

projects.name: Project Boson

projects.name: Project Green Mountain
projects.fight: Conditional use permit pending amid borough-wide resident opposition.

projects.name: Muncy Township data center campus (3 buildings, 100 acres)
projects.fight: The township adopted a nine-month moratorium; residents and supervisors sued in Commonwealth Court over the developer's deemed-approval claim.

projects.name: Henderson Road data center and gas plant

projects.company: QTS; H&H Capital Acquisitions; GW Acquisition Co.

projects.name: Buck Canyon hyperscale site

projects.name: Chandler AI data center (Price corridor)

projects.name: Project Baccara

policies.what: Emporia Question 2: citizen ordinance banning high-impact data centers, defined as over 10 MW peak load or 100,000 gal/day of water; it cannot take effect until a court rules on its validity.
El Dorado: 10-year ban on high-impact data centers and Tier 2/3 battery storage systems, placed on the ballot 5-0 after a court ruling.
Ottawa: ban on data centers over 25 MW, ordered onto the ballot by a judge; a legal challenge is pending.
SB 98 (2025): 20-year sales tax exemption for data centers investing at least $250M; Democratic nominee Holscher calls for a statewide pause.

21 local data center measures in 18 Ohio jurisdictions: 25 MW caps in Conneaut, Defiance, Granville, Oregon, Pataskala, Piqua, Sunbury, Trenton and Upper Sandusky; Urbana 7.5 MW cap; Hubbard full ban; plus Grove City, Perry, Monroeville, Ashville, four Wilmington referendums, and Monroe and Sprigg townships in Adams County.
Proposed statewide constitutional amendment banning data centers over 25 MW; it had about 105,000 of 420,142 required signatures by July 8, and the target moved to November 2027.
Mount Orab six-month data center moratorium.
Augusta Township referendum repealed the 522-acre data center rezoning by about a 9-1 margin.

At least 19 Michigan municipalities had enacted data center moratoriums as of February 2026, including a 12-month moratorium in the City of Saline; a bipartisan one-year statewide pause bill has not been enacted.
Ypsilanti Community Utilities Authority 12-month moratorium on water service to data centers; county commissioners backed local moratoriums.
Port Washington referendum passed, requiring voter approval of TIF districts over $10M; business groups have sued.
Janesville: voter approval required for development of the GM/JATCO site over $450M.
At least 24 Wisconsin communities have adopted data center moratoriums, typically for one year.
Boulder City Question 1: whether to allow data centers in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area.
Advisory measures in Bloomington (moratorium), Chouteau, Granite City, Nameoki and Venice in Madison County, Joliet in Will County, and Morgan County.
Edgewater charter amendment prohibiting new data centers.
Alhambra citywide data center ban measure, plus Monterey Park Measure NDC, a ban on the June 2, 2026 ballot whose result was not confirmed here.
Indianapolis Metropolitan Development Commission approved 6-0 a ban on new data centers through at least Dec 31, 2027.
At least 50 Indiana counties restrict data centers: 32 moratoriums, 14 regulatory ordinances and 4 prohibitions. Marshall's ban is permanent and Starke approved a ban Oct 19.
Gov. Shapiro EO 2026-05 removes data centers from the Fast Track program, bars state NDAs, and withholds state permits until local approvals are in place.
Hazle Township six-month pause on new data center applications, passed unanimously.
Muncy Township nine-month moratorium on processing data center applications.
County Council voted unanimously to ban large data centers on county-owned property.
Moratorium extended 5-2 through Sept 30, 2026.
Unanimous moratorium on new data center proposals through Jan 1, 2027.
Commission voted 4-3 against an outright ban; the existing moratorium runs to year end.
Savannah 155-day moratorium on data centers over 10 MW.
Augusta data center ordinance passed 6-5, banning data centers in residential and agricultural zones and requiring 500-foot buffers.
A statewide moratorium bill failed in the 2026 session; 34 counties and 23 cities have adopted, proposed or are developing data center ordinances or moratoriums.
Six-month moratorium proposals failed 3-2 on Feb 10 and Feb 24, 2026; in March the county tightened development rules.
More than 25 Iowa counties and at least six cities have passed some form of data center moratorium, per ICCI documentation.
Commissioners passed a moratorium of up to one year on new data center permits.
St. Charles city council passed a unanimous one-year moratorium on new data center applications.
Legislature passed a moratorium on facilities of 20 MW or more, which Gov. Mills vetoed; she signed a separate law barring data centers from state tax incentives.
The county adopted new zoning rules restricting future data center development; details were not retrieved because the article page was blocked.

polls.finding: 62% of Iowa voters oppose data centers being built near or in their community; 24% support.
60% say data centers will hurt the environment, 52% cost of living, 46% quality of life; on jobs, 44% negative and 41% positive.
Among 600 likely voters, 18% view data centers favorably and 65% unfavorably.
68% oppose a new data center in their community and 17% support; 55% oppose one elsewhere in Missouri.
Nearly 8 in 10 likely voters oppose data centers, whether anywhere in Maryland or near their community.
55% of Wisconsin voters say the costs of large data centers outweigh the benefits.
63% oppose data centers in or near their community and 27% support, up from 42% opposed in December 2025.
75% of registered voters would oppose a new data center near where they live, up from 42% in August 2025.
71% of U.S. adults would oppose an AI data center in their area, 48% strongly.
64% of Iowa voters oppose more data centers; 30% support.
61% of Kansas voters oppose more data centers; 33% support.

notes: 1) The research stopped early when the shared limit of 200 web searches for this turn ran out; later work only fetched pages already found, which left gaps. There is little or no project coverage for NV, NC, MN, LA, MS, SC, NH and AK, and only one item each for ME, AL and NE. A follow-up message can resume searching, starting with Google's announced Texas sites, Meta's Louisiana and El Paso sites, and NC, MN, SC, NV and MS projects. 2) The premise that Iowa and Kansas polls this month found most voters oppose data centers was not confirmed for October. The Iowa majority-opposition figure, 62% vs 24%, comes from Emerson's August 2026 poll and was cited again by NewsNation on Oct 13. The Kansas figure, 65% unfavorable, comes from an August 13-16 Global Strategy Group memo. No October Kansas data center poll was found. Emerson's Sept Kansas poll had no data center question. 3) FIPS codes were assigned from the standard Census county code list and were not fetched from a source. Counties for Kline Township PA (Schuylkill), Festus MO (Jefferson), Peculiar MO (Cass), Edgewater FL (Volusia) and Alhambra CA (Los Angeles) are inferred from standard geography, not stated in the cited article. 4) The mw field means different things across rows: Homer City's 4,500 MW is the gas plant (about 3,700 MW is for data centers); Comanche Circle's 3,000 MW covers three Sailfish projects; Marana's 750 MW is the top of the first-phase 550-750 MW range; Balico's 300 MW is first-phase IT load. Saline Township has also been reported at $7B and $43B; the table uses $16B from Tom's Hardware, May 2026. 5) Status calls and limits: Abilene is marked operating because one building was live as of Sept 2025. The Salem Township AWS expansion is marked construction, but the confirmed facts are an approved rezoning and an existing 48 MW facility. The statuses for Bessemer AL (Aug 2025), Pittsboro IN (Mar 2025) and Peculiar MO (Oct 2024) are older and were not rechecked. 6) Data Center Watch reports only totals, with no project lists: 75 projects worth $130B blocked or delayed in Q1 2026, and 45 worth $68B in Q2 2026, with 843 opposition groups in 49 states. 7) Sources excluded under the rules: Politico, including a Politico/Public First poll; NYT, including a cited NYT/Siena poll; DDHQ, X and the Star Tribune. Pages that blocked fetching were skipped without workarounds: Detroit News, NPR, US News, CNBC, Statesman, MySA, Yahoo, and a WTOP page whose headline alone was used for Fauquier.
